---
title: "1 and 1L are equal but not identical"
ref: NUM-09
categories: [Numbers]
impact: incoherent
extrait: 'identical(length(1:3), 3)'
reponse: 'FALSE'
attendu: "`TRUE`, the vector does have three elements"
versions: "All"
source: "General R knowledge"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
1 == 1L
identical(1, 1L)
identical(length(1:3), 3)
```
:::

## Why

`==` compares values, after converting both sides to a common type. `identical()` compares objects: the type is part of the object, and `1` (double) is not `1L` (integer).

The pitfall is easy to miss because R does not show the type when printing. `length()` returns an integer, the literal `3` is a double: a test written with `identical()`, or with `expect_identical()` from {testthat}, fails even though both sides print 3.

## The remedy

Write the literal in the right type, or compare the values with a function that ignores the type.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
identical(length(1:3), 3L)
isTRUE(all.equal(length(1:3), 3))
```
:::
